ceramicsEcosystem.community: Berkeley is the old heart of East Bay ceramics: The Potters' Studio, the Berkeley Potters Guild, UC Berkeley's Art Practice ceramics (Cathy Lu, with Ehren Tool running the studio) and the public Berkeley Art Studio. indigenousTraditions.ceramicsHeritage: Berkeley is Huchiun, part of the land of Chochenyo-speaking Ohlone people. Ohlone craft is basketry, not pottery. The West Berkeley Shellmound and Village Site at 1900 Fourth Street, thousands of years old and long buried under a parking lot, was bought and returned to the Sogorea Te' Land Trust in April 2024 with City of Berkeley support.
indigenousTraditions.respectfulEngagement: Support Sogorea Te' Land Trust (Shuumi Land Tax), and eat at Café Ohlone by mak-'amham, where Vincent Medina (Chochenyo Ohlone) and Louis Trevino (Rumsen Ohlone) serve Ohlone foods on the UC Berkeley campus on a seasonal schedule (check makamham.com). The Phoebe A. Hearst Museum of Anthropology holds Native collections with a difficult history; its galleries were closed at last check.

practicalInfo.visaInfo: Rwandan citizens need a US visa: a B-1/B-2 visitor visa for visits, applied for at the US Embassy in Kigali. ESTA and 90-day visa-free entry are only for citizens of Visa Waiver Program countries, and Rwanda is not one. Working or teaching for pay needs a separate status with work authorization (for example an O-1 artist visa or an employer-sponsored visa). US visa rules changed often in 2025-26, so check travel.state.gov and the embassy before applying.
practicalInfo.healthcareAccess: Private, insurance-based system: an uninsured visit to a doctor or emergency room is very expensive. Visitors need travel medical insurance; residents usually get cover through an employer or Covered California. Community health clinics offer sliding-scale care.

Berkeley, California, USA.forWinnie: Berkeley is a town built around making, reading and eating well: The Potters' Studio and the Berkeley Potters Guild are classic East Bay pottery institutions, Stonemountain & Daughter and the Lacis Museum will feed your weaving, and Berkeley Bowl's produce aisles would make any cook happy. The weather is gentler than San Francisco's, with sunny afternoons, but winters are wet and cool (about 15 °C). It's expensive and student-heavy, yet smaller and calmer than the cities around it, and there's Ethiopian food on Telegraph Avenue.

ceramicsEcosystem.community: San Francisco has more community studios than ever, from The Pottery Studio, RedBrick and Artillery in the Mission to small neighbourhood studios like Bisk and Speckle, but firing is almost always members-only and wait-lists are common. Clay mostly comes from Douglas & Sturgess (SoMa and Richmond) or Clay Planet in Santa Clara: Leslie Ceramic Supply has closed. Ways in: the San Francisco Ceramic Artists Guild (founded 2025), ArtSpan and Shipyard open studios, the Loom and Shuttle Guild and Textile Arts Council for weaving, and the Fort Mason craft fairs. Clay by the Bay closed in July 2026, and California College of the Arts will close after the 2026-27 academic year.

indigenousTraditions.ceramicsHeritage: The Ramaytush Ohlone are the original people of the San Francisco Peninsula. Ohlone peoples did not make pottery: their great craft traditions are basketry (coiled and twined, decorated with feathers and shell beads), shell-bead and stone work, and the shellmounds built along the bay over thousands of years, almost all of them destroyed by development.
indigenousTraditions.respectfulEngagement: The Association of Ramaytush Ohlone (ramaytush.org) speaks for Ramaytush descendants, and the city's official land acknowledgment names them; the Muwekma Ohlone Tribe also has ancestral ties around the Bay. If you want to dig local clay, ask first: collecting earth is banned in most parks (GGNRA, state and regional parks), and some sites are culturally sensitive.

practicalInfo.visaInfo: Rwandan citizens need a US visa: a B-1/B-2 visitor visa for visits, applied for at the US Embassy in Kigali. ESTA and 90-day visa-free entry are only for citizens of Visa Waiver Program countries, and Rwanda is not one. Working or teaching for pay needs a separate status with work authorization (for example an O-1 artist visa or an employer-sponsored visa). US visa rules changed often in 2025-26, so check travel.state.gov and the embassy before applying.

Many people live without a car.

San Francisco, California, USA.forWinnie: San Francisco gives you the most clay in the smallest space: a bus ride reaches a dozen studios, and you could buy injera in the Sunset and hear jazz in the Fillmore on the same night. Coming from Kigali's steady warmth, the summer fog will surprise you: a July afternoon here feels like a cool Kigali evening, so you'll want a wool layer all year. The hard part is cost, among the highest rents in the country, which is why many potters live in the East Bay and cross for classes and markets. If you want to teach and be seen, though, this is where many of the doors are.

Oakland, California, USA.practicalNotes: Oakland is the Bay's most energetic clay town right now, and rents are about half of San Francisco's (one-bedrooms averaged about $2,100 in mid-2026, Zumper). BART reaches downtown San Francisco in about 15 minutes. Safety varies block by block, so ask locals before choosing a street.

indigenousTraditions.ceramicsHeritage: Oakland is in the territory of Chochenyo-speaking Ohlone people. Like other Ohlone communities they were basket makers rather than potters, and they built large shellmounds along the bay shore, including the West Berkeley shellmound a few kilometres north.
indigenousTraditions.respectfulEngagement: Sogorea Te' Land Trust, an urban Indigenous women-led land trust co-founded by Lisjan Ohlone leader Corrina Gould, returns land to Indigenous stewardship; many residents pay its voluntary Shuumi Land Tax. The Muwekma Ohlone Tribe also represents Ohlone descendants of the East Bay. The two have different histories, so name each one correctly.

Oakland, California, USA.forWinnie: Oakland might be the most natural fit: a working clay scene with cone 10 gas firing, a residency that centres Black and Indigenous artists, natural-dye classes at A Verb for Keeping Warm, and an Ethiopian and Eritrean community whose coffee ceremonies and injera will feel familiar. It's sunnier and a few degrees warmer than San Francisco, though still cooler than Kigali for most of the year. Rent is about half of San Francisco's and BART crosses the bay in fifteen minutes. It's also a city with real inequality and some rough blocks, so choose your street with local advice.

practicalInfo.healthcareAccess: Private, insurance-based system: an uninsured visit to a doctor or emergency room is very expensive. Visitors need travel medical insurance; residents usually get cover through an employer or Covered California. Community health clinics offer sliding-scale care.
practicalInfo.notes: A small river town on the Sonoma side, about an hour from San Francisco and Oakland. Cheaper than Marin and San Francisco but still expensive; SMART trains help, though daily life needs a car.

foodScene.notes: Farm country on your doorstep: two weekly farmers' markets, wood-fired bread, and cheese from America's oldest cheesemaker in the hills. There's no East African restaurant in town; the nearest injera is in Oakland or Berkeley, about an hour away.

Petaluma, California, USA.forWinnie: Petaluma is a small river town with a real potter's thread running through it: Petaluma Pottery's classes, Forrest Lesch-Middelton's tile studio, Sonoma County's residencies and wood firing, and Fibershed's local fibre and dye movement nearby. Summers are warm (about 27 °C) and dry, but winter mornings are cold (about 4 °C) and foggy, colder than anything in Kigali. It's calmer and cheaper than the cities, though you'd be an hour from Oakland's community and Ethiopian food, and you'll want a car.
